position.summary: The AI Security Engineer implements and evaluates detection methods and security controls, performs threat modeling of AI- and agent-enabled application workflows, analyzes machine-generated traffic together with identity and permission signals, and conducts security testing and remediation verification. The position requires the theoretical and practical application of a specialized body of knowledge in computer science and information security. It is a hands-on, individual-contributor position with no supervisory responsibility.

duties.title: Implement and evaluate detection methods and security controls
bullets: Implement rule-based detection for automated abuse in customer-authorized request, gateway and agent tool-call logs
Build protection and filtering rules fitted to each customer's traffic, such as allow and deny lists, rate limits and access policies for sensitive endpoints
Measure false positives against legitimate traffic and missed detections against labeled abusive activity, and tune accordingly

duties.title: Threat modeling of AI- and agent-enabled application workflows
bullets: Map request flows, actor identities and permission boundaries for each assessed workflow
Identify abuse paths: free-tier and API-key abuse, automated account creation, identity spoofing, agent tool calls beyond granted permissions
Apply OWASP automated-threat guidance and NIST SP 800-218A to test design

duties.title: Traffic, identity and permission signal analysis
bullets: Analyze exported production logs and link traffic to identity and session context, permissions and behavioral signals
Distinguish legitimate automation from abusive automation without treating a claimed identity as verified
Maintain a versioned test set of labeled legitimate and abusive activity

duties.title: Security testing, vulnerability analysis and remediation verification
bullets: Run controlled tests in customer staging environments for repeated abusive requests, identity spoofing and unauthorized data access
Analyze identified vulnerabilities and prepare mitigation recommendations
Verify remediation through regression testing after each fix and release

position.owner_duty_title: Ownership-related activities: customer discovery and sales, investor outreach, administration

knowledge_areas.area: Information security: threat modeling, access control and authorization models, adversarial analysis
Computer networking and web protocols: HTTP and API semantics, sessions, authentication flows, TLS
Algorithms and statistical methods: classification, anomaly detection, measurement of false positives and missed detections
Software engineering: implementation, testing methodology, version control and release practice
Data systems: processing and querying large request and log datasets

why_degree: **The adversary adapts.** Automated abuse is built to evade detection. Designing and evaluating controls against an adversary who responds to them requires formal training in threat modeling and adversarial analysis.

**The analysis concerns identity and authorization.** Determining whether an automated actor is acting within its granted permissions requires knowledge of access control models, authentication flows, and web and API protocols.

**Results are judged statistically.** Whether a detection method works is established by measuring false positives and missed detections, which requires training in algorithms and statistical evaluation.
position.ooh_sentence: The U.S. Department of Labor's Occupational Outlook Handbook states that information security analysts typically need a bachelor's degree in a computer-related field.
